solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Head of college locks position for its senior staff

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only the first letter of college is used

parts.note: locks are tresses of hair

explanation.surface: A college principal keeps their hair in place, or so it seems, in a clue about staff roles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of college' reads as the college principal, but it only supplies the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A professorship at a university or college is called a chair, a post held by its most senior academics.

clue.text: Period drama's central character subjected to no peer pressure

indicators.note: in a down entry, being subjected to something means sitting below it, so the letter goes after

parts.note: a commoner is no peer, so pressure from peers in the nobility sense does not apply to them

indicators.note: the central character of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A costume drama's lead resists the pressure of their peers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Period drama' looks like a costume piece, but 'Period' is the definition; 'peer' is a member of the nobility, not an equal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Common Era is the secular name for the dating period otherwise labelled AD.

clue.text: Go off with naked canoeist?

indicators.note: being naked means losing one's covering, so the outside letters of the word are stripped

parts.note: a canoeist is a paddler

explanation.surface: Imagines what happens when a canoeist strips off.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs that addle go rotten, just as milk is said to go off.

clue.text: Lie about copyright policy

parts.note: re means about or concerning
C is the copyright symbol
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: Someone tells falsehoods regarding a publisher's rules on copyright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie' reads as an untruth but means to lie back.
explanation.definitionFit: To recline is to lean back or lie down in a relaxed position.

clue.text: Old person somehow beginning to improve, right after avoiding hospital care

indicators.note: somehow suggests things are put together in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged
the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of improve is taken
avoiding means doing without, so the hospital letter is removed from the word for right

parts.note: the word right itself is used

explanation.surface: An elderly patient somehow starts to get better and avoids needing hospital care.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a patient recovering outside hospital; 'after' is only a link, and the letters are mixed into one pool before being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Geriatric is used, often disparagingly, as a noun for an elderly person, especially one receiving medical care.

clue.text: Growth of goods to eat in — passable when served up

indicators.note: to eat is to take in, so the goods letters hold the other piece

parts.note: G is short for good, so goods gives two of them

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means brought upwards, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: OK means passable or acceptable

explanation.surface: Talks of food to eat in a restaurant being merely passable when served.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a restaurant review; 'Growth' is a tree, not a business.
explanation.definitionFit: The gingko (usually ginkgo) is a tree, and a tree is a kind of growth from the ground.

clue.text: Faith in generalissimos restored after purging rebellious masses

indicators.note: restored means rebuilt, so the remaining letters are put back together in a new order
purging means removing; rebellious masses means those letters are taken out in no set order

explanation.surface: Belief returns among military leaders once the unruly crowds are cleared out.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the letters of MASSES from GENERALISSIMOS and rearrange what is left, GNERLIIO, to get the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A religion is a system of belief and worship, a faith.

clue.text: Triumph one's driven to celebrate

definitions.meaning: the Triumph ... was a car made by the British maker Triumph in the early 1980s

explanation.walkthrough: 'Triumph' looks like a victory but is the car maker.
explanation.definitionFit: The car bore this model name, and to acclaim someone is to hail or celebrate them.

clue.text: Pragmatic article is in need of editing

indicators.note: a text that needs editing has to be reworked, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A practical-minded newspaper piece still needs revision.
explanation.definitionFit: Realistic means having a sensible, practical view of what is achievable.

clue.text: Policemen reported rather sticky situation?

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, so the word is taken by how it is said

parts.note: cops are policemen

explanation.surface: Police officers have reported being in an awkward predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sticky situation' suggests a tight spot; here it is a place full of sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: A copse is a small wood, a spot crowded with sticks and young trees, hence humorously sticky.

clue.text: Honour nurses taking risks lacking clothing related to treatment

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold closely, so the honour word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a medal is an honour awarded for service

indicators.note: clothing is the outer layer, so without it the word loses its outside letters

parts.note: dicing, as in dicing with death, means taking risks

explanation.surface: A decorated nurse takes risks without protective clothing while treating patients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking clothing' strips DICING to ICIN, which MEDAL 'nurses'.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicinal describes something that has healing properties or is used as a remedy for illness.

clue.text: Winner has tea with politician

parts.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A victor celebrates by having a cup of tea with a Member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Champ is an informal short form of champion, someone who has won a contest.

clue.text: Large spike in approval is preceded by brief career

indicators.note: in signals that the following pieces are placed within the word for approval

parts.note: OK is informal approval

indicators.note: preceded by means the second piece follows the first, so the career word comes ahead of is
brief means cut short, so the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to belt is to career along at high speed

explanation.surface: Reads like a news item: a big jump in approval ratings comes after a short-lived career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large spike' looks like a statistic, a sharp rise in the approval figures, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An obelisk is a tall tapering stone pillar ending in a pyramid point, a monumental spike.

clue.text: Hard Rock Cafe finally faced by one blocking subsidy

indicators.note: faced by means having something in front, so the cafe letter comes after the rest
one piece blocking another sits inside it, like an obstruction in a pipe

parts.note: a grant is a subsidy or financial award
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word cafe

explanation.surface: The Hard Rock Cafe, a restaurant chain, finally meets someone holding up its funding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard Rock Cafe' looks like one name, but it splits after 'Rock'.
explanation.definitionFit: Granite is a very hard igneous stone, a classic example of a tough rock.

clue.text: Resented contest separating half of field

indicators.note: separating means coming between, so the contest word goes into the middle of the other piece
half of means only part of the word survives, here its second three letters

parts.note: to field, as a fielding side in sport, is to defend
to vie is to contest or compete

explanation.surface: Someone was bitter that a match divided a playing area in two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' keeps END, the back half of DEFEND, which VIE is 'separating'.
explanation.definitionFit: Envied means felt jealous of someone's advantages, a resentful feeling.

clue.text: Break up civil riot expressing considerable bitterness

indicators.note: breaking something up scatters its parts, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Police disperse a public disturbance amid furious resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitriolic describes speech that is caustic and filled with bitter criticism.

clue.text: Hound arts graduate that is cursed primarily with doctrinaire manner

parts.note: a hound is a dog
MA is a Master of Arts

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so the opening letter of each of these three words is taken

explanation.surface: A dog is cursed and badgers an arts graduate with dogmatic preaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hound' reads as a verb, to harass, but it is just the noun dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogmatic means asserting opinions as undeniably true, the attitude of a doctrinaire person.

clue.text: Cycling picture screened by commercial channel is authorised

indicators.note: screened by means hidden behind, so the picture piece sits within the channel word

parts.note: a canal is an artificial channel built for commerce

indicators.note: cycling means going round, so the first letter of the picture word moves to the end

parts.note: an icon is a picture, especially a religious one

explanation.surface: A cycling film is shown on a commercial television channel with official approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commercial channel' looks like ITV-style broadcasting but is a canal; 'Cycling' turns ICON into ONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Canonical means accepted as authoritative, like the books officially approved for scripture.

clue.text: President stops oil company producing black fluid

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so the president word goes inside the company name

parts.note: Esso is a brand of the ExxonMobil oil company

explanation.surface: A head of state halts an oil firm's production of crude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black fluid' suggests crude oil; it is coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is strong coffee served without milk, a dark black drink.

clue.text: Broadcaster is keen to provide accommodation for star

indicators.note: providing accommodation means housing, so the answer is lodged within these words

explanation.surface: A television company is eager to put up a celebrity during filming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star' looks like the celebrity guest, but it is the printed symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: An asterisk is the small star-shaped typographical symbol used to mark footnotes.

clue.text: Two artists quietly drinking dry type of gin

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the dry piece goes inside the artists and quiet letters
two signals that the artists abbreviation appears twice

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
TT, teetotal, means dry or not drinking
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Two painters quietly sip a dry gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' looks like the spirit, which suits 'drinking' and 'dry', but here a gin is a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is a trap for catching animals, and a rat trap is one such device.

clue.text: Rasher guards last to observe warning signal

indicators.note: to guard is to surround protectively, so the rasher word encloses the other letter

parts.note: a rasher is a slice of bacon

indicators.note: the last to means the closing letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A slice of bacon is kept safe by the final person on watch for a warning.
explanation.definitionFit: A beacon is a fire or light set up on high ground to warn of danger.

clue.text: Gnome mounted horse to cross gorge

indicators.note: to cross means to span over, so the horse word goes around the gorge word
in a down entry, mounted means going up, so the word reads from the bottom

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
to pig is to gorge or eat greedily

explanation.surface: A garden ornament rides a horse across a ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gnome' looks like a garden figure, but it means a pithy saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnome in the literary sense is a short maxim or aphorism, much like a witty saying.

clue.text: Outfit with a fluid approach

definitions.meaning: to outfit is to provide with equipment
in a supple, flexible manner, the adverb from supple

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the rare adverb of supple, not the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To kit out someone is to provide them with goods, and supply also means flexibly.

clue.text: Chat inanely following introduction of this platform

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the chat word comes behind the introductory letter
the introduction of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: to witter is British slang for talking at length about trivial things

explanation.surface: People chatter mindlessly once this social media site is launched.
explanation.definitionFit: Twitter was a social media service, the kind of online venue called a platform.

clue.text: Dispenser of alcohol has raised tense issue

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means moved higher, so the tense letter goes to the top

parts.note: an optic is a measuring device fixed to an upturned bottle in British pubs
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A bar dispenser has caused a tense problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a subject for discussion, an issue under consideration.

clue.text: Fabulous animal that's product of agricultural college?

parts.note: uni is a short form of university, a college
corn is a crop, an agricultural product

explanation.surface: Asks whether a mythical beast could be bred at an agricultural college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'product of agricultural college' reads as one phrase, but splits after 'agricultural'; the college piece goes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A unicorn is a legendary horse with a single horn, a creature of fable.

clue.text: Tender assassin?

definitions.meaning: to tender is to put forward or present something
to off is slang for kill, so a killer is whimsically one who offs; the question mark flags the invented sense

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a made-up agent noun from the slang verb, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To tender a bid is to propose it, and a hit man would be a killer in slang.

clue.text: Cultured pearl is less vivid

indicators.note: a cultured pearl is grown artificially, so the word cultured hints that these letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A farmed pearl has a duller lustre than a natural one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cultured pearl' reads as one phrase, but 'Cultured' is the signal to rearrange PEARL.
explanation.definitionFit: Paler means lighter in colour, so less intense or vivid.

clue.text: Concession opening shortly is hardly raising awareness

parts.note: a sop is a concession made to appease someone

indicators.note: shortly means in brief, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an orifice is an opening

explanation.surface: A shop opening early is said to be doing little to make people notice it.
explanation.definitionFit: Soporific means inducing sleep, the reverse of making anyone more alert.

clue.text: Row about company call terminating early, ending in disarray

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: terminating early means finishing before the end, so the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to phone is to call

indicators.note: the ending in a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: An argument over a business phone call that ended early leaves things in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel but means a noisy din.
explanation.definitionFit: Row in the sense of a loud din matches cacophony, a harsh jumble of noise.

clue.text: Good spirits falling short of ecstasy

indicators.note: falling short of means lacking something, so the ecstasy letter is taken away

parts.note: morale is the spirits of a group
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: High spirits that do not quite reach euphoria.
explanation.definitionFit: Moral as an adjective means ethically good or virtuous.
